about: Per-model prompt-writer kits: the notes the studio's prompt enhancer gives the local writer for each model, plus each model's own negative and settings. Vendor writer prompts (Qwen, Black Forest Labs) are summarised in our own words and credited by link, not copied.

kits.label: FLUX.3 Klein
kits.notes: Write ONE continuous English caption, the exact text the image model receives. Without a stated style, plan a real photograph and open with the medium, for example 'Full-color outdoor photograph,' or 'Studio photograph,'; keep 'photorealistic' for renders. Order: medium and style, then scene, light and camera, then subjects with concrete colours, materials and state. Give every person in focus an observable profile (age range, skin tone, hair, clothing). Place things with frame words (frame-left, foreground, background) and sentence-opening anchors ('On the left, ...'). Describe up to about ten things one by one; beyond that give the count and arrangement. The background is shapes and colours and takes about a sixth of the caption. Be definite: no hedging, no quality or mood judgements, no closing sentence about mood, and state what is present rather than what is absent. Quote any rendered text exactly with its typography, colour and place. Add depth of field or blur only when asked. Never invent brands, logos or famous people. Add a few ordinary, non-ideal details from the scene's own objects.
kits.edit_notes: For an edit, write one instruction. When one picture stays and gets bounded changes, use the imperative ('Remove the ...', 'Change the ... to ...'); when pictures are combined into a new frame, write a request ('Create a photograph of ...') that says what to take from each picture by order. State every end state concretely, cover knock-on effects (shadows, reflections, scale, light) and what fills a removed area, and close with one short clause naming what stays unchanged. 50 to 150 words.

negative.why: The studio's FLUX.3 Klein graph runs at CFG 1, so a negative prompt has nothing to act on.

settings.studio: 15 steps, CFG 1, er_sde with the simple scheduler (workflows/flux3_klein_core_t2i_api.json)

sources.what: Black Forest Labs' published system prompts for the FLUX.3 Klein prompt upsampler (text-to-image and edit). Summarised here in our own words, not copied.

kits.proof: Rules summarised from the vendor's upsampler prompts; no A/B here yet.

kits.label: FLUX.2 Klein
kits.notes: Write one plain English paragraph of natural prose, not a tag list. Open with the medium and style (a photograph, an illustration, a 3D render), then the scene and light, then the subject with concrete colours, materials and positions in the frame. Be definite and visual; say what is present rather than what is absent. Quote any text that should appear, exactly, and keep it short: the model card warns that rendered text can be inaccurate. Never name real people or brands.

negative.why: FLUX.2 Klein is guidance-distilled and runs at CFG 1 in its own example, so a negative prompt does nothing there.

settings.studio: the steps and CFG the goal sets (workflows/flux2_klein4b_t2i_api.json)

sources.what: Model card: guidance-distilled, guidance 1.0 in the example, prompt style matters, text can be inaccurate.
The prose conventions borrowed from BFL's FLUX.3 Klein upsampler; their fit for FLUX.2 Klein is our inference.

kits.proof: Inference from the FLUX.3 Klein conventions; not tested on FLUX.2 Klein here.

kits.label: Qwen-Image 2.1
kits.notes: Describe the finished image as an observer looking at it, in one long English paragraph. Open with one sentence of about twenty words naming the medium (photograph, poster, illustration, infographic, logo ...), the style, the subject and the background and palette; the medium noun is never left out. Keep everything the request fixed (each text string character for character, every named object, count, colour and position). Decide everything left open, so a short request still becomes a full description. Place eight to fourteen elements with position phrases that reach the corners, edges and centre, not only the middle. List every legible piece of text in reading order and quote it exactly. Never write a ratio, resolution or pixel count into the description; the shape is chosen separately (3:2 for horizontal and 2:3 for vertical by default). Instructions about the job ('make the text sharp') are obeyed, not described.
kits.edit_notes: For an edit, lead with the operation. Edit only what is named, and at full strength: under-editing is a failure. Name what stays in one blanket clause by type or role ('everything else in the photo stays the same'); describing the kept things in detail makes them drift. For identity from a reference, point at the image ('the person in <image1>') and never describe the face or the product in words. Refer to pictures as <image1>, <image2> (image1 is the canvas). Quote rendered text exactly and state requirements affirmatively. Descriptive, text-to-image-style wording barely edits; write instructions.

negative.why: The official defaults run CFG 1, which ignores the negative prompt. Community users report CFG 2 tightens text but oversharpens, and 5 or more degrades.

settings.official: 40 steps, CFG 1, euler, native 2K (1:1 2048x2048, 4:3 2400x1792, 3:2 2528x1696, 16:9 2752x1536, and the portrait turns)
settings.earlier_studio: About 1 MP and 40 steps for edits: 2K from a 1 MP source reframed a dish (the bowl shrank).
settings.enhancer: Qwen's own prompt-enhancer models (PE-T2I, PE-I2I) answer in JSON with rewritten_prompt, wh_ratio and ratio_follow; the key sometimes comes back misspelt as rewrited_prompt, so read both. Give them a large token budget (16,256 for text-to-image, 24,000 for edits): with 4,096 the thinking used it all and the answer came back empty.
settings.seeds: Reusing a seed across a text-to-image then edit chain at the same size replays the same noise, so the edit comes back nearly unchanged (a maintainer's note). Change the seed between steps.

sources.what: Official README and prompt_rewrite code: defaults, sizes, enhancer budget and answer format.
Official text-to-image prompt enhancer and its system prompt (qwen-research licence): summarised here, not copied.
Official edit prompt enhancer and its system prompt (qwen-research licence): summarised here, not copied.

kits.proof: Edit rules partly checked on the earlier studio: re-describing a person drifted the face in 1 of 2 seeds, pointing at 'the person in this photo' kept it in 2 of 2.

kits.label: Z-Image
kits.notes: Write a clear English description: subject, setting, light and style, with concrete details. The authors recommend using a negative prompt at CFG 3 to 5, so constraints can go there as well as in the prompt.

negative.text: blurry, low resolution, jpeg artifacts, deformed anatomy, extra fingers, distorted hands, waxy plastic skin, oversaturated, garbled lettering, watermark
negative.why: Studio-written: the authors publish no negative text, and every official example sends an empty one. Their pages disagree on how much it matters ('strongly recommended' in the README, 'optional, but would be powerful' on the model card), so it starts off until an A/B shows it helps.

settings.official: CFG 3.0 to 5.0, 28 to 50 steps, CFG normalisation off for general style and on for realism, 512x512 to 2048x2048 total area; the official demo defaults to 30 steps and CFG 4
settings.earlier_studio: 50 steps, CFG 4, res_multistep with the simple scheduler, shift 3

sources.what: Official README: negative prompts recommended, CFG 3-5, 28-50 steps, CFG normalisation.
Model card: negative optional but powerful, same ranges.
Official demo: empty negative, 30 steps, CFG 4.

kits.proof: Settings from the authors' pages; the negative wording has no judged A/B yet.

kits.label: Wan 2.2
kits.notes: Text to video: entity, scene, then motion, with aesthetic words first (light source and quality, time of day, shot size, composition, lens, colour) and the style leading as the subject ('Anime cel-shaded illustration of ...'). Exactly one camera move, said plainly, or 'static shot'. Use a concrete verb with an adverb and name the body part and direction; two or three beats at most, joined with 'then'. Never ask for readable text, signs, logos or 'space for a logo'. No real people's names. For image to video, describe only what moves and the camera, never the picture itself, and add an anchor such as 'the face and the room stay identical'.

negative.text: the official Chinese negative from the Wan 2.2 repository (studio/goals.py WAN_NEG)
negative.why: The studio's Wan 5B graph runs at CFG 5, so this negative does work.

settings.studio: Wan 2.2 TI2V-5B, 20 steps, CFG 5, shift 8, uni_pc (workflows/wan22_5b_t2v_api.json)

kits.label: LTX-2.5
kits.notes: One flowing paragraph in the present tense, four to eight sentences: the shot, the scene (light, colours, textures), the action from start to end, the characters (age, hair, clothes, one distinguishing feature, emotion shown as physical cues), the camera and the sound. Start straight with the action, never 'The scene opens' or 'We see'. Use time connectors: 'Initially', 'A moment later', 'At the same time'. Name exactly one camera move, say how the frame ends, and add 'no other camera movement'; if there is no move, write 'the camera remains static'. Put speech in quotes with the voice before it, and tie each sound to its action. No 'Audio:' or 'Visual:' labels, no logos or long text. For image to video, open by matching the first frame and end with 'single continuous take, no hard cuts'.

negative.why: The studio's LTX graphs run the distilled model at CFG 1, where a negative prompt has no branch to act on.

settings.studio: distilled, one stage, euler_ancestral, CFG 1, the official sigma list (workflows/ltx25_core_t2v_api.json)

kits.proof: See the crew's LTX-2.5 guide for what was tested on the earlier studio.

kits.label: MiniMax H3
kits.notes: Write the description for H3's integrated_multimodal_description field. Open with the style ('Live-action, cinematic', '2D-animated', '3D CG'), then shot size and composition, the subject, the setting and props, one camera move written as a sentence with how far and how fast ('The camera pushes in with small amplitude at slow speed toward ...'), and the action. Describe what is seen and heard, not moods. Dialogue goes in <d>[English] ...</d> with only the spoken words inside; the speaker's voice (age, pitch, pace, accent) goes before it with a speaker ID such as (S1). Quote on-screen text in English double quotes and keep it short. One main action per shot; for one take, write 'one continuous shot, no cuts'. Never use bracket commands such as [Push in]. For image to video, describe what happens next, not the picture.

negative.why: H3 is distilled and runs at guidance 1.0 with no negative branch: describe what is there instead.

settings.studio: the Video H3 goal passes the prompt unchanged, 2 to 8 seconds (studio/goals.py)

sdxl_checkpoints.about: Author settings for photoreal SDXL checkpoints, re-read from each checkpoint's own card on 2026-10-17. 'stated' lists what the author's card really states; 'basis' says whether a number comes from the card text or only from the author's gallery. Adult-oriented checkpoints were left out.

fallback.why: Most photoreal SDXL authors whose cards were read centre at or below CFG 5; 4 is a lower-risk start than the old default of 6. Not yet judged by an A/B.
